question: How does Jude identify his relationship to Jesus Christ and James, and what threefold spiritual identity does he attribute to believers?
opt1: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called
opt2: Jude, the high priest of the circumcision, to them that are circumcised by the law, and justified by works
opt3: Jude, an apostle to the Gentiles, to them that are enlightened by philosophy, and governed by civic magistrates
opt4: Jude, a prisoner in Rome, to them that have escaped persecution, and gathered in subterranean catacombs
correct: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called
explanation: Jude introduces himself humbly as Christ's servant and the brother of James, addressing the elect as sanctified by the Father, preserved in Christ, and effectively called into fellowship. Jude 1:1 (KJV) - "Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called:"

question: While Jude was giving all diligence to write concerning the common salvation, what urgent pastoral imperative compelled his letter?
opt1: Instruct you that ye should negotiate theological compromises with surrounding pagan guilds
opt2: Exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints
opt3: Exhort you that ye should withdraw completely from civil society into monastic seclusion
opt4: Command you that ye should establish armed defenses to resist imperial Roman decrees
correct: Exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints
explanation: The infiltration of dangerous heresies shifted Jude's intent from a general treatise on salvation to a passionate rallying cry for believers to vigorously defend the once-for-all delivered apostolic faith. Jude 1:3 (KJV) - "Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints."

question: How does Jude describe the corrupt lifestyle and core theological error of the ungodly men who crept into the church unawares?
opt1: Imposing rigorous Pharisaic dietary laws, and enforcing circumcision upon Gentile converts
opt2: Demanding celibacy from all church members, and forbidding the ownership of private property
opt3: Turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ
opt4: Practicing animal sacrifices at local altars, and restoring the Aaronic levitical priesthood
correct: Turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ
explanation: These deceptive apostates perverted divine grace as a license for moral debauchery (antinomianism) and denied the sovereign lordship of God and Jesus Christ. Jude 1:4 (KJV) - "For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ."

question: What three historic examples of divine retribution does Jude recount to demonstrate that God punishes unfaithfulness and rebellion?
opt1: The builders of the tower of Babel, the army of Pharaoh at the Red Sea, and the camp of Israel at Kadesh-barnea
opt2: The house of Eli at Shiloh, the army of Sennacherib outside Jerusalem, and the priests of Baal at Mount Carmel
opt3: The kingdom of Babylon under Belshazzar, the Philistines at Gaza, and the citizens of Nineveh under Jonah
opt4: The generation saved from Egypt that believed not, the angels that kept not their first estate, and Sodom and Gomorrha suffering eternal fire
correct: The generation saved from Egypt that believed not, the angels that kept not their first estate, and Sodom and Gomorrha suffering eternal fire
explanation: Jude presents three sober precedents of divine judgment: unbelieving Israelites destroyed in the wilderness, rebellious angels bound in everlasting chains, and Sodom and Gomorrha suffering the vengeance of eternal fire. Jude 1:5-7 (KJV) - "I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not. And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day. Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire."

question: How did Michael the archangel conduct himself when disputing with the devil about the body of Moses, in contrast to arrogant false teachers?
opt1: Durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee
opt2: Summoned twelve legions of angels to cast the devil immediately into the bottomless pit
opt3: Uttered vehement personal curses against Satan, mocking his fallen angelic dignity
opt4: Compromised with the devil by dividing Moses' earthly remains between heaven and earth
correct: Durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee
explanation: Even the mighty archangel Michael exhibited reverent restraint toward fallen dignity, refraining from abusive insults and leaving judgment in God's hands with the words, 'The Lord rebuke thee.' Jude 1:9 (KJV) - "Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation, but said, The Lord rebuke thee."

question: What threefold Old Testament triad of apostasy does Jude invoke to pronounce solemn woe upon corrupt teachers?
opt1: Woe unto them! for they built the altars of Jeroboam, worshiped the calves of Bethel, and sacrificed to the host of heaven
opt2: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core
opt3: Woe unto them! for they followed the rebellion of Absalom, coveted the vineyard of Naboth, and walked in the sins of Manasseh
opt4: Woe unto them! for they consulted the witch of Endor, touched the ark like Uzzah, and offered strange fire like Nadab and Abihu
correct: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core
explanation: False teachers replicate Cain's murderous self-righteousness, Balaam's mercenary compromise for financial gain, and Korah's defiant revolt against God's appointed authority. Jude 1:11 (KJV) - "Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core."

question: What five vivid metaphors from the natural world does Jude deploy in verses 12-13 to depict the spiritual bankruptcy of false teachers?
opt1: Tares among the wheat, wolves in sheep's clothing, leaven in three measures of meal, salt without savor, and broken cisterns
opt2: Locusts consuming the harvest, vipers hiding in rocks, thorns choking the seed, foxes spoiling vineyards, and withered figs
opt3: Spots in your feasts of charity, clouds without water, trees twice dead plucked up by the roots, raging waves foaming shame, and wandering stars
opt4: Vultures gathering over carcasses, dry bones in the valley, deaf adders stopping their ears, roaring lions, and fading grass
correct: Spots in your feasts of charity, clouds without water, trees twice dead plucked up by the roots, raging waves foaming shame, and wandering stars
explanation: Jude's vivid imagery captures their hypocrisy: hidden reefs at love feasts, rainless wind-blown clouds, barren uprooted fruit trees, shameless stormy waves, and wandering stars doomed to eternal darkness. Jude 1:12-13 (KJV) - "These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever."

question: What ancient eschatological prophecy spoken by Enoch, the seventh from Adam, does Jude cite regarding the Lord's coming in judgment?
opt1: Behold, the sun shall be darkened at midday, and the moon turned into blood before the great day of the Lord
opt2: Behold, a fiery chariot shall descend upon the mountains of Israel, and all pagan empires shall be overthrown
opt3: Behold, an angel shall seal the servants of God in their foreheads before the four winds hurt the earth
opt4: Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them
correct: Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them
explanation: Enoch's ancient antediluvian prophecy confirms that the Lord will descend with myriads of His holy ones to execute decisive judgment upon ungodly deeds and defiant speech. Jude 1:14-15 (KJV) - "And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him."

question: What four essential spiritual disciplines does Jude urge upon believers to maintain their personal preservation in the love of God?
opt1: Building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life
opt2: Fasting twice every week, paying tithes of mint and anise, observing sacred new moons, and avoiding all Gentile trade
opt3: Memorizing the genealogies of the patriarchs, debating theological puzzles, performing public penances, and taking monastic vows
opt4: Seeking secular political influence, petitioning Roman governors, amassing church wealth, and erecting protective walls
correct: Building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life
explanation: Jude outlines the vital pathway of spiritual stamina: doctrinal edification on the holy faith, Spirit-empowered prayer, abiding within divine love, and eager anticipation of Christ's eternal mercy. Jude 1:20-21 (KJV) - "But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life."

question: With what renowned, triumphant doxology does Jude conclude his letter, extolling God's preservation of His saints?
opt1: Now unto the holy angels that guard your assemblies, and preserve your bodies from the persecution of Rome, be praise
opt2: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, to the only wise God our Saviour
opt3: Now unto the company of the apostles that founded the church, and established the traditions of the elders, be honor
opt4: Now unto the monarchs of the earth that grant religious peace, and protect the assemblies of the saints, be dominion
correct: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, to the only wise God our Saviour
explanation: Jude concludes with one of Scripture's most magnificent doxologies, celebrating God's power to preserve believers from stumbling and present them unblemished before His glorious presence with boundless joy. Jude 1:24-25 (KJV) - "Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen."
